title: Best Dehumidifier for 500 Sq Ft (2026): Right-Sized Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for 500 Square Feet
dek: Five hundred square feet is too much room for a mini and too little for a basement brute. Here’s how to size it right — and the units that fit.
description: The best 500 sq ft dehumidifier picks by dampness: 20- to 32-pint models from Midea, Hisense, hOmeLabs and AirPlus, plus the math for rooms and basements.
intro: Shopping for a **500 sq ft dehumidifier** sounds simple until you see the range on offer: thumb-sized minis that promise to “cover” your room, and 50-pint basement units that would dry it to a crisp. For a space of about 500 square feet — a studio apartment, a large primary suite, a two-car garage or a small basement — the right answer is almost always a compact compressor unit rated somewhere between 20 and 32 pints a day.

Exactly where you land in that range depends on how damp the space is, not just how big it is. Below, we walk through the sizing math, show what 500 square feet looks like in real rooms, and pick the dehumidifiers that fit each situation, from a mildly muggy bedroom to a basement corner that seeps after rain.
topPicksLead: For most 500-square-foot rooms, the **Midea Cube 20** is the best dehumidifier: it’s honestly rated under the 2019 DOE test, one of the most efficient small units you can buy, and it holds an exact humidity target from your phone.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for 500 sq ft

blocks.text: We don’t lab-test. We compare capacity under the 2019 DOE procedure, ENERGY STAR listings for efficiency and annual energy use, manuals for drainage and humidistat options, CPSC recall records and patterns in owner reviews. Every pick here also has a verified Amazon listing.

For this size, we prioritized right-sizing over raw power. An oversized unit costs more to buy, takes up more floor space and short-cycles; an undersized one runs nonstop and never reaches the target. So we chose one strong pick for each level of dampness, then weighted efficiency, humidistat precision and drainage.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 500 sq ft dehumidifier

items.label: A DOE 2019 pint rating
items.text: Compare DOE figures only. Listings that headline 50, 60 or 80 pints for a compact unit are usually quoting older or saturated-air tests.

items.label: A compressor, not a Peltier
items.text: Thermoelectric minis remove ounces a day. At 500 square feet you need a compressor unit that removes pints.

items.label: A set-a-number humidistat
items.text: Choose a unit that lets you dial in 45% or 50% and cycles off once it gets there.

items.label: ENERGY STAR
items.text: A small unit can run hundreds of hours a season. Certified models use noticeably less power for the same water.

items.label: Drainage that fits the room
items.text: In a bedroom, a large tank is fine. In a basement or garage, look for a gravity-hose connection near a floor drain.

items.label: Low-temperature operation
items.text: For a garage or basement that drops below about 60°F, look for auto-defrost so the coil doesn’t ice up.

sections.heading: What size dehumidifier for 500 sq ft?

blocks.text: Start with how the space behaves, then adjust. These ranges follow our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/), narrowed to a single 500-square-foot space.

blocks.text: When to move up a size

items: **Ceilings above 8 feet.** A vaulted 500-square-foot room holds as much air as a much larger standard room.
**A moisture source nearby.** A shower, washer, dryer vent or aquarium adds water every day.
**No door.** If the space opens onto a hallway or stairwell, you’re dehumidifying the whole connected area; see our [1,000 sq ft guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-1000-sq-ft/).
**Cool temperatures.** Below about 60°F, compressor units remove less water, so a basement or garage needs extra headroom.

blocks.text: Garages are the outlier: big doors let humid air in every time they open, and winter temperatures fall below where most units work well. Our [best dehumidifier for garage](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-garage/) guide covers that case in depth.

sections.heading: Getting the most from a dehumidifier in a 500 sq ft room

items: Put it near the middle of the room or the dampest wall, with 6–12 inches of clearance on every side.
Keep the door and windows closed while it runs, or you’re drying the outdoors.
Run it on high for the first day or two, then let the humidistat take over at 45–50%.
Check a separate hygrometer across the room; built-in sensors read the air right next to the unit.

blocks.text: More placement rules are in our [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) guide.

For a typical 500-square-foot room, a 20- to 22-pint compressor dehumidifier is the sweet spot, and the **Midea Cube 20** is the one we’d buy first for its efficiency and app control. Step up to the **Hisense 25-Pint** if you see condensation, or the **hOmeLabs 32-Pint Wi-Fi** for a small basement or garage that’s truly wet. Skip the minis at this size — and skip the 50-pint boxes too, unless the space is part of a larger open area.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for 500 square feet?
faqs.a: For a moderately damp 500 sq ft room, a 20- to 22-pint unit under the 2019 DOE rating is enough. Choose about 25 pints if you see condensation and 30–35 pints if the space has seepage or is a cool basement or garage.

faqs.q: Is a 20-pint dehumidifier enough for a 500 sq ft room?
faqs.a: Yes, if the room is musty but not wet and has standard ceilings. The Midea Cube 20 handles a 500 sq ft bedroom or office comfortably. If it runs almost nonstop without reaching your target, the room needs a bigger unit.

faqs.q: Is a 50-pint dehumidifier too big for 500 sq ft?
faqs.a: Usually. It will dry the room, but it costs more to buy, takes more floor space and cycles on and off more often. A 50-pint unit makes sense only if the 500 sq ft space is very wet or opens onto a larger area.

faqs.q: Can a mini dehumidifier handle 500 sq ft?
faqs.a: No. Most thermoelectric minis are rated for about 1,200 to 2,200 cubic feet, while a 500 sq ft room with 8-foot ceilings holds about 4,000. Use a mini in a closet or bathroom and a compressor unit for the room.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a 500 sq ft basement?
faqs.a: A basement of that size is usually cooler and damper than a bedroom, so we’d choose around 30 pints, such as the hOmeLabs 32-Pint Wi-Fi, and run a hose to a floor drain. If there’s seepage, the [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) picks go bigger.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier in a 500 sq ft room?
faqs.a: Not much. The Midea Cube 20 is rated at 249 kWh a year by ENERGY STAR — roughly $40 at typical U.S. electricity rates. Our [dehumidifier electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) explains how to estimate your own cost.
